subject: spectral bat
title: A Bat With a 1-Meter Wingspan Hunts Birds and Carries Them Home

scenes.text: Something leaves piles of feathers under one tree. Every night.
The spectral bat of Central and South America. Wingspan close to a meter, about 180 grams. The largest carnivorous bat on Earth.
It hunts birds, and finds them by smell, not by echoes. Doves, cuckoos, even a 150 gram pigeon, nearly its own weight.
Then it carries the kill home to a hollow tree. One roost in Costa Rica held the remains of 86 birds from 18 species in a single year.
Inside, a family of up to five hangs in one clump. The male wraps the mother and pup in his wings while they sleep.
The feathers under the tree are what's left of dinner.

description:
A bat with a wingspan close to a meter hunts birds, then flies them home to a hollow tree.
The spectral bat is the largest carnivorous bat on Earth, about 180 grams, and it locates sleeping birds by scent rather than echolocation; its prey ranges from 20 to 150 grams, almost its own weight. Both parents bring food back to the roost, where a family of up to five hangs together and the male wraps the female and pup in his wings. Under one Costa Rican roost, researchers collected the feathers of 86 birds from 18 species in a year.
Which other animal would you never guess was a predator?
first_comment: A spectral bat may need only one bird every two or three nights. Which bat fact surprised you most?
